summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Dung Ngoc Duong earned a PhD from Boston University in 2001 under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries, as well as Trashichöling, under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he held professorships at Minzu University and Tibet University.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He taught Sanskrit at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, and Sanskrit College and University.
Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Durga Prasad Dikshit studied under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian who completed his studies at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta.
Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London, completed his PhD at UCLouvain in 2018, and served as a research scholar at UCLouvain.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo, and Khenpo Rinchen. In 1990, he became a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965) studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under teachers including the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse. He directed the Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse (born 1961) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sakya College and SOAS, training under Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, the 16th Karmapa, and the 41st Sakya Trizin.

Dörte Kamarid is an Indology and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

E. E. Evans-Pritchard (1902–1973) studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at the LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and served as a professor at Oxford from 1946 to 1970.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010), a Tibetology and Buddhist studies specialist, studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith Colleges, Utah, Washington, and Leiden. He served as a consultant for the Library of Congress and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

E. J. Rapson (1861–1937) was an Indologist and linguist educated at St John's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum, was Professor of Sanskrit at University College London, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1906 to 1936.
E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed his education at the University of Cambridge, the University of Chicago, and the University of Paris.

E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985), an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he became principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer (born 1941) is an Indology and archaeology specialist who completed his PhD at the University of Basel. He served as director of Museum Rietberg from 1972 to 1998 and president of the Rietberg-Gesellschaft.

Eberhard Sandschneider (born 1955) is a sinologist who studied and earned his PhD at Saarland University. He held professorships at the University of Mainz and Free University of Berlin, and was a director at the German Council on Foreign Relations.

Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) studied linguistics and history/archaeology at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, and Jena, and was a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (1875–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Charles University and the University of Washington, with traditional training under Shrinarayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held appointments at Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin.

Edgar H. Sturtevant (1875–1952) was a linguist who was educated at Illinois College and Indiana University. He held academic posts at Columbia University from 1908 to 1920 and at Yale University from 1923 to 1943.
